b10e968b76e4af51.subject: What makes an agent actually read a cold email from a screenwriter?
b10e968b76e4af51.body:
View this post on the web at https://stephenfollows.com/p/what-makes-an-agent-actually-read-a-cold-email-from-a-screenwriter

A few weeks ago I published the first half of my conversations with the people who read cold scripts for a living [ https://substack.com/redirect/5157a301-4893-430b-80fd-ff063a6ef802?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. I spoke to 38 agents, managers, assistants and junior execs on which credentials actually get a script read. 
We learned that getting your script on the annual Black List or winning the Nicholl Fellowship can turn heads, but that few other competitions or laurels help.
So let’s say you’re not one of the lucky few who have achieved those rare accolades - how else can you get an agent to read your script?
Today I’m sharing the advice these same people gave to aspiring screenwriters. 
Overall, the sentiment was not warm towards cold approaches. One put it like this:
I pretty much delete all cold emails automatically unless I’m bored, which is rare.
Yikes.  But just because it’s hard doesn’t mean it’s impossible. In fact, if we look at the numbers another way, we can see that, like Jim Carrey’s character in Dumb and Dumber [ https://substack.com/redirect/d9c7d1e0-cf56-4dd5-a51d-e1510d3c229b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], I’m saying there is a chance.
So what can you do in your cold approach to be one of the select few?  In my interactions with these gatekeepers, a number of actionable steps emerged.
Personalise, because they can tell
Do your homework
Never use AI
Hook ‘em fast
Do not oversell - they check
Make it short, professional, and polite
Tell YOUR story
Let’s look at each in a little more detail.
Rule one: Personalise, because they can tell
The most common theme by a distance was personalisation, or the lack of it. A cold query that could have been sent to anyone gets deleted on sight.
Immediate pass if there is zero customization to me personally, ie I can tell someone has sent the exact same query to myriad reps and they’re throwing spaghetti at the wall.
And they really can tell. The mechanics of the mass-blast betray the sender in ways writers may not realise:
Please don’t copy and paste the same email to every manager... we can absolutely tell (especially when our names and companies are in different fonts than the rest of the email).
Some described wanting a genuine point of connection, a mutual professor, the same festivals, a shared former colleague, and added a detail that should give any name-dropper pause. If a writer claims to know one of their clients, they will sometimes text the client to check.
Rule two: Do your homework
Know who the company is and what it does, include the logline, a short synopsis and the practical details, and be clear about what you are actually asking for. 
They need to do research about what we do. 
One assistant even offered a workaround for companies that officially take no cold queries at all:
If the person put the work in to find my personal email address NOT JUST LINKEDIN I will at least read a logline and go from there.
Several also said the smartest queries arrive with more than a bare script. As one expert put it:
You always love to see a short sizzle or something extra, before I just commit myself to 120 pages of a stranger’s script... at the minimum showing that there’s more of a vision beyond the pages usually helps.
Rule three: Never use AI
I would hope this one was obvious, but just for the avoidance of doubt - don’t use AI.  Anywhere, ever. 
I’m not anti-AI, but if you’re saying you’re a professional writer, then even a whiff of generative AI in “your” writing or emails is a killer. (And the suspicion of AI use can even lose you a $2 million book deal [ https://substack.com/redirect/bd3cc072-3eca-4beb-9697-fc40364e6cf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], as we saw last week).
As one person put it:
And never ever use AI to write your cover note. One can pick that a mile off.
Rule four: Hook ‘em fast
Even a perfect email only buys you a few pages of attention. We already learned [ https://substack.com/redirect/5157a301-4893-430b-80fd-ff063a6ef802?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] that just 8% read the whole script. 13% have decided by page five, and two-thirds have decided by the end of page ten.
So the opening pages have to do what your email did and earn the next minute of their time. One agent with more than ten years in the business went further than any page count:
I read the first line. Not so good is lots of description to start the script. Less is more!
And a junior exec made the same point about the query itself:
I rarely respond to cold queries, if at all. If anything an undeniable logline can get me interested.
It’s a layered approach - the logline earns the click, the first line earns the first page, and the first ten pages earn the rest. You’re fighting uphill at each stage.
Rule five: Do not oversell - they check
Inflating a minor credential reads as naivety, the opposite of what the writer intended.
Bigging up more low key prizes, or interest from irrelevant producers, too much... it shows a naivety or lack of industry understanding.
And the checking is not hypothetical. One manager described their own diligence:
What turns me off is if the query says they’re “in development” on a number of projects and easy research shows those projects are, at most, optioned.
Rule six: Make it short, professional, and polite
This is a lesson we should all apply in our everyday lives, but it applies even more when cold-calling industry gatekeepers with your script.  As one put it: 
A long, verbose, cryptic query letter is an immediate pass. Concise and professional, and material-forward!
Long emails with typos, loglines that strain to be funny, flowery begging, all named as instant passes. 
One exec boiled the ideal email down to a formula:
Short and concise is good. Pitch the hook, why this project is UNIQUE, relevant attachments and background, and a very short reason the writer is compelling as well.
This etiquette does not stop at the first email. One agent, a generous reader who gets through whole scripts and advanced three cold writers last year, drew a single hard line:
I will immediately pass if I get a rude chase up.
There was even a warning for writers who do have representation and query anyway. More than one reader said an already-repped writer reaching out alone is a red flag rather than a plus. As one agent put it, the first question in their head is simply: 
Why doesn’t their rep reach out?
And several respondents added that their company will not read genuinely cold queries at all, often for legal reasons, and route everything in through a referral instead. 
Rule seven: Tell YOUR story
Many of the respondents said that the query needs to tell them where you are going, not just what you have written. One said they wanted writers who have:
…achieved momentum on their own and know why they’d now want an agent.
That word momentum came up in different forms across the answers. It does not have to mean much. One manager with over a decade in the business set the bar at:
I will read if they’ve been recommended by a producer or have produced something (even if only a short film, taster, etc)
Another put the same idea in the past tense:
My default is to pass immediately - the few I have responded to were because they had some level of success already with produced credits or competition wins.
This matches the numbers from my previous article [ https://substack.com/redirect/5157a301-4893-430b-80fd-ff063a6ef802?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], where a produced credit was the second-strongest signal of all, behind only a referral. A short film, a taster, a staged reading, a web series: anything.

85c91916b68ed5eb.subject: The Invention of the Streaming Movie Star
85c91916b68ed5eb.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.statsignificant.com/p/the-invention-of-the-streaming-movie

Intro: Adam Sandler, Small-Screen Star
In 1999, Adam Sandler was the biggest movie star in America, if such a title exists. His irreverent humor and goofy voices propelled low-budget comedies like The Waterboy and Big Daddy to $375M and $465M in global box office (adjusted for inflation), despite Roger Ebert’s thorough disdain for both films—and the disapproval of nearly every other major critic.
From there, Adam Sandler was box office gold, with a run of hits that includes 50 First Dates, The Longest Yard, Click, I Now Pronounce You Chuck and Larry, Bedtime Stories, Grown Ups, and Just Go with It. Each movie cleared $100M, and each movie was savaged by critics.
And then his box office dominance began to falter. Following the back-to-back disappointments of That’s My Boy and Blended, Sandler gradually retreated from theatrical exhibition, eventually signing a lucrative deal with Netflix through his production company, Happy Madison.
Since then, Adam Sandler has mainly been a streaming movie star, barring a handful of exceptions—most notably all-time ulcer-inducer Uncut Gems. Over the past 5 years, Sandler has starred in a handful of films that feel borderline nonexistent despite being watched by tens of millions of people: Spaceman, Hubie Halloween, and You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah. All real, all number one on Netflix, and all subsequently memory-holed.
Sandler may be the foremost example of a streaming movie star: an A-list actor whose career has become increasingly oriented around the small screen. And while streaming films have existed for less than fifteen years, they have already produced a recognizable cohort of performers, led by a hodgepodge of one-time box-office draws and ascendant television actors.
So today, we’ll explore the rise of the streaming movie star, identify the performers who have embraced this newfangled format, and examine the forces that drove these actors away from theaters in the first place.
The Rise of the Streaming Movie Star
When you consider the streaming movie’s roots—such as the afterschool television special, the made-for-TV movie, or the Hallmark Christmas film—what Netflix and its competitors have built is actually quite remarkable. Hallmark, a greeting-card-company-turned-cable-network, cultivated a stable of D-list celebrities whose theatrical careers had long faded (or never really existed), while streamers have replicated this same model but on a grander scale, with A-list actors whose box-office appeal has only recently begun to wane.
As such, the actors with the most prolific streaming careers are box-office stalwarts from the 1990s and 2000s who are only a few years removed from their commercial peak, including Mark Wahlberg, Adam Sandler, Ben Affleck, and Eddie Murphy.
At the same time, making a lot of movies for Prime Video or Netflix does not necessarily make someone a “streaming movie star.” An actor like Adam Sandler or John Cena may simply be prolific, with some of their projects landing on streaming platforms.
So, according to this fledgling classification (that we are defining in real time), what puts the “streaming” in streaming movie star?
My argument is that this distinction comes down to a balance between theatrical and straight-to-streaming releases. Since 2019, only 8% of A-list actors with multiple leading roles have appeared exclusively in streaming movies, while another 22% have worked across both formats but tilt more heavily toward streaming. Taken together, both groups could reasonably be classified as streaming-movie performers.
To see this distribution in action, we can construct a Venn diagram separating streaming-only performers from theatrical mainstays based on their post-2018 movie output. On the theatrical side, we find Margot Robbie alongside a handful of action stars like Gerard Butler and Keanu Reeves. On the streaming end of the graphic, we get an odd mixture of one-time box-office draws, along with somebody named Sofia Carson (who we’ll return to in a second).
For the most part, the actors who lean toward streaming are well-known performers with careers that predate cord-cutting, with the exception of Sofia Carson, who belongs to an emergent class of actors made famous by Netflix who exclusively star in films that go straight to Netflix. Other performers who fit this amorphous category include Millie Bobby Brown (aka Eleven from Stranger Things), Joey King, and Zoey Deutch.
These are performers whose fame was either cultivated almost entirely through streaming or whose careers veered into the streaming ecosystem at an early stage. However, cases like Millie Bobby Brown and Sofia Carson are the exception, since the prototypical Netflix movie star is usually much further along in their career, having already established their box-office bona fides in the 1980s, 1990s, or 2000s.
This trend rests on a straightforward contract between platform and actor: a streamer leverages a performer’s considerable (yet fading) commercial capital; in return, the actor gets money, visibility, and a steady supply of work. It’s a fair trade. And yet the discourse surrounding straight-to-streaming movies often treats the participation of well-known actors as a kind of moral failure. This logic usually goes something like this: If these actors are so rich and famous, why can’t they simply choose better projects? Why settle for a format that is slowly eroding the very institution that made them famous in the first place—the theatrically released movie?
That may be true for some actors, particularly those sitting in the middle of our Venn diagram. But many performers have far less agency than we assume. The deeper I got into this analysis, the more I came to see the Netflix-performer relationship in reverse: actors don’t choose streaming so much as streaming chooses them.
Consider the share of streaming-only movies split out by genre: leading parts in comedy and romance skew toward Netflix, while action and horror movies are more likely to be released theatrically.
This helps explain why action stars like Keanu Reeves and Jason Statham remain firmly on the theatrical-only side of our Venn diagram, while comedic actors like Eddie Murphy and Adam Sandler have been absorbed into the broader Netflix ecosystem.
If you’re a comedy star from the 1980s or 1990s—or an emerging actor frequently cast in rom-coms, like Sofia Carson or Zoey Deutch—then streaming movies constitute the lion’s share of roles you’re offered.
Let’s say you fall into one of these buckets and you’re headed for a career of small-screen stardom on Netflix, Prime Video, or Hulu. Is that really such a bad thing? Does choosing a streaming-only movie over a glitzy theatrical release consign you to cultural irrelevance?
There is indeed a notoriety tax associated with a streaming release (versus a premiere in theaters), but it’s smaller than you might expect. When we examine how long a lead actor’s Wikipedia page trends amongst the site’s daily top 100 entries following a movie release, we find a meaningful—but hardly enormous—gap between theatrical and streaming films.
With the exception of 2020, when nearly every movie was a streaming movie, straight-to-streaming releases see a fairly consistent 12% drop in search interest—a penalty that feels surprisingly modest given the format’s subpar cultural reputation.
And if the goal is simply to remain visible, keep making movies, and continue collecting paychecks, then starring in a Prime Video production doesn’t seem like such a drastic compromise.

f7f8117276d490ed.subject: Is New York ‘Habibi City’? Gen Z’s Mental Health Loophole. Plus. . .
f7f8117276d490ed.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.thefp.com/p/is-new-york-habibi-city-plus

It’s Wednesday, August 12. This is The Front Page, your daily window into the world of The Free Press—and our take on the world at large. Today: Liel Leibowitz on why New York will never be “Habibi City.” Maya Sulkin talks to the white-collar Zoomers who feel owed their mental-health leave. And much more.
But first: Welcome to “Habibi City.”
The city formerly known as the Big Apple is now “Habibi City.” So declared a viral cover story in New York magazine this week, announcing the arrival of a new cadre of Middle Eastern residents building community and defining contemporary New York by resisting “xenophobia, Islamophobia, and Zionism.”
We wanted to make sense of this trend ourselves, so we turned to Liel Leibovitz, himself an immigrant from the Middle East to the United States.
He moved here, he writes for us today:
. . . for the one and only reason anyone should ever come to America: Because I believe it, firmly and passionately, to be the greatest nation ever endowed by God with the mission of spreading liberty and light to a benighted world, and because I consider it the honor of a lifetime to partake in the solemn work of making America ever greater. Apparently my fellow Middle Eastern immigrants have very different feelings.
Don’t miss Liel on “Habibi City” and why the viral essay gets the story of New York, and immigration to America, exactly backward.
—The Editors
MORE FROM THE FREE PRESS
THE NEWS
Four crew members were killed [ https://substack.com/redirect/dac617b8-6f1f-4366-83bb-f0b80e06292c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] by a suspected Houthi strike on an Egyptian-owned cargo ship in the Red Sea yesterday as tensions mounted in Middle Eastern waterways. Separately, a U.S. missile struck a second ship bearing the Panamanian flag near the Gulf of Oman as it tried to evade [ https://substack.com/redirect/0efac7cf-8886-4d54-94d9-eb2ef8caaa4d?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] the region’s American blockade.
Per President Trump’s request, Russia has released [ https://substack.com/redirect/9ee78798-700c-4352-ad2b-5d5851f16933?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] U.S. Marine Robert Gilman, who had been imprisoned since 2022 and whose health had badly deteriorated in custody. Russia made no public demands in exchange for Gilman, who according to Russian state media was arrested and jailed for drunkenly kicking a police officer.
Donald Trump hid in an airline catering container to surreptitiously escape Turkey during last month’s NATO summit after intelligence officials learned of an Iranian threat to his life. Two senior U.S. officials confirmed Monday that the elaborate ruse [ https://substack.com/redirect/cf8a18ba-b8aa-4086-9563-7a0f89632818?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] involved using Air Force One as a decoy while Trump was whisked to another aircraft.
A Cleveland father set a new world record [ https://substack.com/redirect/0e8ae133-fd9f-458d-af96-a8870bc4437f?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] over the weekend for the fastest mile run while pushing a stroller: 4 minutes and 17 seconds. Guinness World Records has yet to certify the new record, which beat the previous one by nearly nine seconds.
Nobody won Monday night’s $905 million Powerball jackpot, sending the estimated prize for Wednesday’s drawing to $1 billion. It is now the eighth-largest [ https://substack.com/redirect/ed304281-fc68-40a7-88f6-5e0db9d3f0d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] jackpot in Powerball history.
The judge in charge of suspected UnitedHealthcare CEO shooter Luigi Mangione’s trial announced yesterday that jurors will remain anonymous [ https://substack.com/redirect/c51e0ac1-fdb9-4cd3-a4c1-08d90591e760?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], citing prosecutors’ concerns of intimidation from Mangione’s supporters. “The People have documented threats, harassment, and exposure of personal information directed at individuals perceived as connected to the case, including witnesses and others,” the judge wrote in an order published Tuesday.
Colombian authorities are searching for survivors [ https://substack.com/redirect/ff8a9e6e-09b9-4382-a870-fdba1ae25251?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] of a 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck the South American country on Monday, leaving many trapped under debris. The death toll has risen to 181, with over 2,500 injured, according to president Abelardo de la Espriella.

Unsubscribe https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cudGhlZnAuY29tL2FjdGlvbi9kaXNhYmxlX2VtYWlsL2Rpc2FibGU_.NzPWZwkbQf4J2BpLavSG1-JokdEFw4EUsXZqZhvJ66U?

Caption:

**Good morning, AI enthusiasts, and welcome to the 5,596 new readers who joined us yesterday. **That memo you just worked with Claude to write? It might soon carry an invisible signature that says so. 

Anthropic just quietly detailed the rollout of invisible watermarks that label everything its Claude models touch, and, like most features forced onto the world, a lot of users aren’t happy about it. 

_**Reminder:**__ Our next live workshop is today at 2 PM EST. Join University Instructor Nate Grehek for “Your AI Reset”, a beginner catch-up on the latest terms, tools, and setups to get better results in your work. __[RSVP here](https://app.therundown.ai/live/your-ai-reset-workshop)__. _

———————————————————————————

**In today’s AI rundown:**

* Anthropic adds AI watermarks to Claude outputs

* Grok Bot is the latest AI agent teammate build

* Use ChatGPT to build a custom Mac shortcut system

* xAI co-founder’s River banks $1.1B for personal AI


----------

----------
**LATEST DEVELOPMENTS**


----------

----------
###### ANTHROPIC

#### 🔎 **_[Anthropic adds AI watermarks to Claude outputs](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16266773-how-claude-marks-ai-generated-content)_**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cb0f5d88-9ca3-4044-9465-ac74f147644f/claudewatermark.jpg?t=1786482235)
Caption: Image source: Images 2.0 / The Rundown

**The Rundown: **Anthropic just [published](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16266773-how-claude-marks-ai-generated-content) a support page detailing plans to embed invisible watermarks in text, code, and file outputs from Claude, putting the EU AI Act’s transparency rules into practice globally across its user base.

**The details:**

* Text and code generated by new Claude models will carry a hidden watermark that carries through when copied and pasted outside the platform. 

* Files will get the same C2PA provenance standard label that is already used across the industry to mark AI-generated media. 

* Older Claude models will need to be ‘retrofitted’ to include the labelling, with models shipping after Aug. 2 having the tool built in.

* Anthropic is also planning to [release](https://x.com/trq212/status/2087258090169414008?s=20) its own detection tools and noted that a mark shows content was “==processed by Claude”, not necessarily fully authored. ==

**Why it matters: **The move is a polarizing one, with takes ranging from positive to dystopian and overreaching. Anthropic isn’t alone in signing the AI Act, with OpenAI, Google, Meta, and others (notably absent: xAI) likely needing to navigate the issue as well. For the negative camp, the case for private and open models continues to grow. 


----------

----------
###### TOGETHER WITH [YOU.COM](http://YOU.COM)

#### 🔎 **_[Why ‘bolt-on’ search breaks in production](https://you.com/resources/ydc-apis?utm_campaign=28104480-The%20Rundown%20Q3&utm_source=external-newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_term=rundown_primary_715&utm_content=rundown_primary_715)_**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/12328a3a-c12a-4d3f-bf68-10e85d931053/unnamed__44_.jpg?t=1786470953)
Follow image link: (https://you.com/resources/ydc-apis?utm_campaign=28104480-The%20Rundown%20Q3&utm_source=external-newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_term=rundown_primary_715&utm_content=rundown_primary_715)
Caption: 

**The Rundown:** Search results go stale, so teams bolt on an API, add a scraper, wire up a parser, and hope it holds. Yeah, it works in the demo, but then it breaks under production load six months later. This guide from [You.com](https://you.com/resources/ydc-apis?utm_campaign=28104480-The%20Rundown%20Q3&utm_source=external-newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_term=rundown_primary_715&utm_content=rundown_primary_715) explains why treating research as simple retrieval is the wrong frame, and what a purpose-built stack looks like instead.

**What you'll learn:**

* Why general-purpose search hits 93% SimpleQA accuracy but still fails high-stakes workflows

* The difference between an API that returns results and one that answers questions

* How teams reclaim 6–12 months of time with a single endpoint

* What finance, legal, and compliance workflows need beyond web search

Stop treating research as retrieval. _[Download the guide](https://you.com/resources/ydc-apis?utm_campaign=28104480-The%20Rundown%20Q3&utm_source=external-newsletter&utm_medium=email&utm_term=rundown_primary_715&utm_content=rundown_primary_715)_.


----------

----------
###### SPACEXAI

#### 👋 _**[Grok Bot is the latest AI agent teammate build](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot)**_

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5f82b889-1502-49c1-b0a1-07f871247c38/grokbot.jpg?t=1786482700)
Caption: Image source: xAI

**The Rundown: **SpaceXAI and Cursor just [rolled out](https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot) Grok Bot, a new beta app that turns Grok into an iMessage-style chat of teammates that have their own dedicated computers, work autonomously, and can access everyday apps just like a real user. 

**The details: **

* Bots are able to coordinate with each other independently or in group chats, and learn from workflows and improve over time.

* New specialist agents can be generated by Bots inside a job or receive handoffs from another worker, with work continuing 24/7 without a laptop open.

* Bots can also access websites and apps on a user’s behalf and observe and create workflows to automate tasks. 

* The beta covers iPhone and Mac, Windows, and Linux desktops for SuperGrok Heavy and top Cursor tiers, with Elon Musk [saying](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2087233507370147920?s=20) access will expand soon.

**Why it matters: **The group chat is becoming a top form factor for running teams of agents. [OpenClaw](https://app.therundown.ai/courses/launch-your-openclaw-from-scratch) and Hermes already live in messaging apps, and Jack Dorsey's [Buzz](https://app.therundown.ai/guides/build-project-room-humans-ai-agents-buzz-tutorial) built a Slack rival where agents are channel members. Grok Bot feels like a middle-ground version built for the masses (if the price comes down significantly).

ed500b90506d0637.subject: The Problem With Peach
ed500b90506d0637.body:
View this post on the web at https://linguasinica.substack.com/p/the-problem-with-peach

Launched at the start of the sweltering summer, the Chinese short drama “The Girl Who Was Laid Off [ https://substack.com/redirect/5f1da467-f86f-4184-ae0a-424bcd5feea0?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]” (被裁掉的女孩) spread like wildfire on the short video platform Douyin (抖音), China’s homegrown version of TikTok. The show’s star, Fang Taozi (方桃子), or “Peach Fang,” rode the show’s success to personal fame by playing the relatable role of the morally centered small-town girl trying to reach her dreams in the big city. By late July, as the show topped 200 million views [ https://substack.com/redirect/ccc3009a-2fcc-47d9-939b-5dbf66e1b9bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], and Fang’s Douyin account [ https://substack.com/redirect/b5c06d59-fb6f-4117-9931-8ea81298ce22?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] was closing in on half a million followers [ https://substack.com/redirect/651fe437-4cbd-46ac-8716-00bd4ae9ba91?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. This made her product promotion royalty as an influencer, commanding a rate of more than 258,000 yuan, or roughly 36 thousand dollars, for any video above 60 seconds.
It seemed that nothing could break the dream — until last week, when Fang Taozi began promoting NUT NUT Look [ https://substack.com/redirect/e901cdaa-bfe2-4413-b1f2-4540adbda612?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] brand contact lenses for an Anhui manufacturer. “I wore them all day long,” she declared [ https://substack.com/redirect/2b63c8db-3e42-463d-ba19-649d79a4cd81?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] in a promotional video, “and it was comfortable the whole time!”
The problem: Fang Taozi may command a very real six figures, but she is an artificial influencer generated by state-of-the-art AI. She has no physical body. Nor does she have any real concept of comfort and discomfort.
Should she be remarking on human experience at all?
As the promotional video had Fang Taozi trending on social media  [ https://substack.com/redirect/5b1117fc-dc22-41cd-8116-f5f0a561ae97?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]— ”How can she test these?” asked one user [ https://substack.com/redirect/387b2c7f-df35-4175-ba94-daa40bfb08b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]; “She doesn’t even have eyes!” — these were the questions raised by Beijing Business Today (北京商报), a business newspaper published under the state-run Beijing Daily Newspaper Group. In a commentary [ https://substack.com/redirect/f052b11e-48f7-4dc1-a3d2-a4faba47ea60?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] stating the obvious, that AI characters do not have bodily experiences and cannot wear, feel, or evaluate physical products, the paper questioned Fang’s authority and the credibility of the marketers. “Advertisements may be able to fabricate appearances, but they cannot fabricate the reality of consumption,” the paper wrote.
There were legal blind spots as well, the outlet reported, drawing on the analysis of real-life lawyers. Virtual images created with artificial intelligence could not be legal persons, they said, and therefore could not qualify as “endorsers” (广告代言人) under Chinese law [ https://substack.com/redirect/a714e990-aaec-4a89-a69c-2bced42143c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. Moreover, under Chinese regulations, the colored contact lenses sold by Anhui Huaxin Enterprise Management Co., Ltd., the makers of NUT NUT Look, would be considered Class III medical devices, which under advertising laws cannot be promoted by endorsers.
Convincing Bruises
The Fang Taozi discussion this month is sure to be the first of many that explore the implications of a world in which corporations and other institutions and entities can impersonate individuals in an AI-driven world.
These days, the dreams can seem startlingly real. Amid the more than 220,000 AI dramas that aired in China during just the first half of this year — 90 percent  [ https://substack.com/redirect/81177907-b707-4bff-904d-878db067204d?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]of them failing to draw audiences — Fang Taozi stood apart because of how unpolished and authentic she appeared on her social media page. Her makeup altered between posts, leaving her convincingly bare-faced or smudged after what were supposedly long and tiring days. She had real apparent skin texture, including moles and tired circles under her eyes. Such fictional imperfections made her more convincing to her audience.
So how does the very authentic looking Fang Taozi, trying to make it as a model in the big city, connect to the real world?
Fang Taozi is the creation of a small team led by a writer-director  [ https://substack.com/redirect/05483ad3-7c9c-4bcf-8a3a-c8a883b2c642?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]identified by the pseudonym “Feifei Fei” (菲菲飞). She is managed as an AI talent by the show’s production company, Guangzhou-based My Film & TV Media Co. (广州我的影视文化传媒有限公司), founded in 2019 and majority owned (75 percent [ https://substack.com/redirect/f2c0ddca-7001-4d8b-859b-ce437fea8bac?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]) by Fang Fei (方菲), the real-life former model [ https://substack.com/redirect/7952e97e-e24d-47aa-b0d9-41bed5bda057?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] behind the “Feifei Fei” pseudonym, who once modeled for fashion magazines like ViVi (昕薇 [ https://substack.com/redirect/671ad290-93e3-40cf-8dcb-a62541e416d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]). My Film, which also offers videography and business consulting services, is 25 percent owned by Guangzhou Thirteen Culture Communication Co., Ltd. (广州十三文化传播有限公司), which calls itself one of China’s “top content and e-commerce MCN platforms.” MCNs, or “multi-channel networks,” are companies that manage, package and monetize a growing range of content creators such as livestreamers, influencers and video creators whose content is distributed on services like Douyin, the social e-commerce platform RedNote (小红书 [ https://substack.com/redirect/6f02104d-a364-447f-88f6-7ef6fb9dc143?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]), the short-video platform Kuaishou (快手 [ https://substack.com/redirect/b06fb6f1-9f29-4659-b461-734f758c9602?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]) and Weibo.
The fictional Fang Taozi, the young woman trying to realize her dreams, will of course not see a single yuan of the revenue generated by successes of “The Girl Who Was Laid Off,” which was reportedly created with the help of LibTV [ https://substack.com/redirect/a3eec9c3-bae8-4b08-bfa7-69267fd6ccfc?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], an AI video-making service that allows users [ https://substack.com/redirect/c75ab01a-1688-49e1-b338-b14a9a6ef204?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] to submit a story concept and receive an AI-generated film. Those earnings will fly directly into the accounts of My Film and its two shareholders, once the platforms have taken their share. There will be no need, as is standard with human influencers, to pay commissions out to talent agencies or managers.
The problem with “Peach Fang” is one that is not unique to China, and that will continue to be a topic of discussion, debate — and probably regulation. AI influencers such as Lil Miquela from Brazil  [ https://substack.com/redirect/c2d8de16-cf58-4f8d-821e-7dfe872ea4d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]and Rozy from South Korea [ https://substack.com/redirect/7173794c

090eb0e1f5746a6d.subject: You Think Modern Dating’s Awful? Then Fix It.
090eb0e1f5746a6d.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.thefp.com/cp/211072057

It’s widely understood now that dating apps have destroyed romance, and Gen Z is  struggling to couple up. We’ve published a [ https://substack.com/redirect/fefb9add-5ef1-4087-90b5-5a2ecc8ae914?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] few [ https://substack.com/redirect/eaa167b0-c08b-49c1-a6c3-3604c505f068?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] stories [ https://substack.com/redirect/25fab09c-8a6a-46bf-bff4-bfd97a9012f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] about how this happened—but here at The Free Press we’re also frustrated by the pessimism we see, everywhere, when it comes to the pursuit of love. The New York Times declares “Gen Z Can’t Afford a First Date [ https://substack.com/redirect/8a693257-cd0c-4040-862a-3f8b9e1a9ec9?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]” (ever heard of a walk in the park!?) and “Gen Z-ers Are Ditching Sex. They Might Be Onto Something [ https://substack.com/redirect/27ee00a4-0ee9-4dcb-8890-575560693707?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]” (on what? Libido-crushing medication!?). The Cut writes [ https://substack.com/redirect/ffcfe08b-405b-4d99-89cf-5fa85f5cf44c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] that “heterosexual women have reached a breaking point.” Celibacy is glamorized. Our fear is that, if you say the search for love isn’t worth it, young people come to believe it.
And they give up on one of the greatest joys life has to offer.
Plenty of our columnists have injected some romantic optimism into our pages. Kat Rosenfield wrote, “Stop Saying Dating Is Terrible. [ https://substack.com/redirect/22d26ab7-23e9-4508-9e01-0c9f78b0a711?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]” Larissa Phillips declared: Bring back matchmaking [ https://substack.com/redirect/b8d9d7f0-59f3-4dbc-bce9-0d93d7166351?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]! Arthur Brooks explained how to make dating apps work for you [ https://substack.com/redirect/7d9c1f4c-8e2d-4b3d-abb0-cfb5e3bb97e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. And for today’s feature, Kara Kennedy—who, lest we forget, married a man she’d known a few months [ https://substack.com/redirect/75b209dc-973d-4020-b109-17092878da03?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]—interviewed half a dozen post-app dating pioneers, young people who decided that just because Tinder is terrible, they didn’t need to give up on dating completely. Instead, they got creative, inventing new ways to track down The One . . .
While reporting, she spoke to Jake Kozloski—founder of Keeper, an AI matchmaker—who gave her a scoop we think is representative of the dating crisis. He told her that Hinge had been interested in acquiring his company, but took issue with their mission [ https://substack.com/redirect/59cfd871-4ab3-46b2-85e3-846f73cb7f9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]—which is, controversially, “to give everyone on Earth the opportunity to marry the right person.”
During negotiations, Kozloski said, “I ended up getting a stern call from someone on their team saying that they read our blogs and did not like that they were pro-marriage, as they felt that was a value judgment they weren’t comfortable making.”
It’s almost as if the aim of the apps was never to get people coupled up for life—but rather, to keep us swiping. Read on to meet the young people with other ideas.
In April of this year, 22-year-old Erin St. Gull printed out a hundred copies of a one-page document [ https://substack.com/redirect/31df8aa2-2c9a-4972-8d90-23a6cf831b4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] and hung them up around Toronto. She calls it a “dating doc,” and in it, she lays out what she needs: marriage; kids; someone, male or female, who is in their late 20s or early 30s and who, preferably, can make her feel excited about life. She also includes what she can offer potential suitors: fertility and youth. She writes that she is extremely smart—and that she can “say this with little pretension as it is the one most provable trait I can claim to have”—as well as “philosophically inclined [and] ruthlessly committed to reason.”
She is also, as you can probably tell, incredibly self-starterish. St. Gull  recognizes, like most of her generation, that the modern dating landscape is broken. But instead of waiting around for someone vaguely acceptable to swipe right, she is willing to put herself out there and scour continents to find the one.
She left Toronto shortly after covering the city with posters, returning to her native France, but on the way she embarked on a 13-city tour of Europe, “a big part” of which was “trying to find the person.” She went to an effective altruism [ https://substack.com/redirect/cb6792a0-6828-4946-81da-9f631566e338?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] conference, conscious that there would be, she told me, “a high concentration of eligible bachelors and bachelorettes in this circle . . . so I knew to scan the room.”
For St. Gull, dating apps are just “one channel,” and one that often doesn’t lead to much.
“At some point,” she said, “my relationship with dating apps shifted from ‘I’m trying to find someone on here,’ to, ‘I am using this purely for entertainment, and on the off chance that someone comes along and is actually interesting, I’m going to talk to them.’ ”...

bf30744ddb98633a.sender: Today's Global Threads from Peter Frankopan <peterfrankopan@substack.com>
bf30744ddb98633a.subject: Europe's Long, Hot - and Dangerous - Summer
bf30744ddb98633a.body:
View this post on the web at https://peterfrankopan.substack.com/p/europes-long-hot-and-dangerous-summer

It has been a long, hot summer. 
Western Europe has just recorded its hottest June and July on record, with a new intense heatwave pushing temperature towards 40C in the UK today.
Wildfires have swept across southern and central Europe, with several countries suffering their worst year for burnt land in decades. A couple of weeks ago, there were fears that cities like Bordeaux and Madrid might be evacuated - or worse.
When I wrote The Earth Transformed, I warned about rising global temperatures, about elevated risks forest fires and about Day Zero coming for cities of the near future. It seems we are closer that I had thought.
Today’s post, however, is about a different kind of rising temperature in Europe. 
Over the last few days, a series of troubling incidents has uncomfortable questions about whether a concerted campaign of sabotage, espionage and hybrid warfare has begun - and that the scenario that many European security services have been warning about for some years has entered a more dangerous phase.
I won’t ask you to enjoy; but I hope you will find it interesting.
The most worrying episode took place at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany last Monday night (3/4 August). 
A small FPV (first-person-view) drone appeared inside a restricted area close to Ukrainian Antonov An-124 transport aircraft. 
According to reports, the drone was not carrying out surveillance, but was an attack device, armed with a substantial amount of high explosives, linked to a detonator. 
Initial reports suggested that one of the nearby Antonov aircraft was loaded with ammunition; German authorities subsequently clarified that the aircraft had recently carried military ammunition from France eastwards via Leipzig, but had returned empty. That might be even be true; any which way, had the device exploded by the aircraft, the results could have been spectacular...

45fd62db5e0fb8ef.subject: La canicule bat 2003, les pompiers restent sans moyens
45fd62db5e0fb8ef.body:
View this post on the web at https://alexispoulin.substack.com/p/la-canicule-bat-2003-les-pompiers

Un jet-ski rouge glisse sur l’eau de Brégançon pendant que les pompiers font grève sans une ligne dans les journaux subventionnés, et que 33 000 climatiseurs promis aux hôpitaux tombent en panne au pire moment de la canicule. Ce contraste n’est pas un hasard de calendrier : c’est le résumé exact de ce que la France regarde, et de ce qu’elle devrait regarder à la place.
Le jet-ski rouge et le pays qui crève de chaud
Brégançon, année après année, le même rituel : jet-ski, lacrymo sur la plage, dispositif de sécurité disproportionné pour deux personnes qui n’ont pas d’amis, seulement des agents. Cette année le jet-ski est rouge, et Paris Match, propriété de Bernard Arnault comme Le Parisien, en fait sa couverture avec la componction d’un service de presse officiel. L’article vante les « ultimes chantiers » du quinquennat, électrification, fin de vie, interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de quinze ans, comme si gouverner consistait à cocher des cases avant de partir en vacances. Les voisins de Brégançon dressent un bilan que même Trump, en pleine éclipse regardée sans lunettes, n’aurait pas osé signer. Et à quelques milliers de kilomètres, Marco Rubio débat du régime alimentaire de Robert Kennedy Jr à la télévision plutôt que de politique étrangère, tandis que Mark Zuckerberg fait du free fight sur un ponton flottant contre des adversaires payés pour perdre. Le loisir des puissants sert partout la même fonction : occuper l’écran pendant que le reste brûle.
« C’est pas ses copains parce qu’il n’a pas d’amis. »
▶ 0:00 — La chanson satirique sur les vacances de Macron [ https://substack.com/redirect/ba3856d3-0423-4edc-9667-606e85a0b0ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 15:16 — Paris Match: le retour du jet-ski de Macron à Brégançon [ https://substack.com/redirect/233cb382-9681-48ba-9d69-a8a7a778a5b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 36:36 — Rubio parle régime pendant que Zuckerberg boxe sur un ponton [ https://substack.com/redirect/50f514cd-caff-4baf-9075-ba5e5b1ec26c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 45:39 — Pompiers en grève, Macron flingué à Brégançon, éclipse sans lunettes [ https://substack.com/redirect/02001ddb-2031-4b81-b3e5-adc12d535aad?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
La succession se joue en famille, la mise en scène aussi
Gabriel Attal, Édouard Philippe, Bruno Retailleau : le même numéro de Paris Match dresse leurs portraits dictés par l’entourage présidentiel, avec ce vocabulaire de cour, « le boss », « le PR », qui devrait alerter n’importe quel lecteur sur qui écrit vraiment ces lignes. Jean Castex, lui, reste indéboulonnable à la tête de la SNCF, preuve qu’on peut rater un mandat et garder un strapontin doré. Dans le même numéro, une autre mise en scène : Raphaël Glucksmann et Léa Salamé photographiés en Corse dans la maison de famille du premier, amour et simplicité version paparazzade organisée. Léa Salamé continuera Quelle époque! mais plus le 20 heures si son compagnon se présente à la présidentielle, drôle de façon de garder les mains propres devant les caméras. Un deepfake grotesque a ensuite tenté de salir ce couple avec une fausse voix d’Edwy Plenel à l’accent russe accusant Salamé de vouloir acheter des articles favorables ; l’affaire, démasquée, vaut plainte de Glucksmann pour protéger la présidentielle. Ce que je retiens surtout : si vous lisez Paris Match sans distance, vous êtes déjà poreux à ce genre de fabrication.
▶ 23:40 — Attal, Philippe, Retailleau, Castex: qui succédera à Macron ? [ https://substack.com/redirect/cfb972b0-3f3f-4726-bdd6-7a8dc46a886a?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 28:27 — La paparazzade Glucksmann-Salamé en Corse décortiquée [ https://substack.com/redirect/abd9798a-3677-4f64-bc42-701e527f4a59?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 33:05 — Le faux scandale Salamé-Glucksmann fabriqué par Moscou [ https://substack.com/redirect/23eab692-ce37-42be-8e6e-08fd60126ccc?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Ce que coûte la canicule, ce que cache la dette
Monique Barbut chiffre le manque à gagner budgétaire de la canicule à 10-15 milliards d’euros. Les 33 000 climatiseurs promis aux hôpitaux par Stéphanie Rist tombent en panne ou n’ont jamais été livrés, un chiffre que la presse régionale préfère taire derrière ses pleines pages consacrées à l’éclipse. François Bayrou, lui, vient expliquer que la totalité de l’impôt sur le revenu ne suffirait plus à payer les seuls intérêts de la dette. Belle démonstration venant de l’homme dont la carrière politique calamiteuse n’a jamais rien coûté qu’à nous, de la dette, une faillite, et personne pour lui présenter la facture. Ajoutez à cela les 678 000 comptes fiscaux piratés sur le site des impôts, une fuite passée sous silence par les grands médias, et vous avez le tableau complet d’un État qui protège mieux ses communicants que vos données personnelles.
« Combien nous a coûté la carrière politique calamiteuse de François Bayrou ? Rien. De la dette, une faillite. »
▶ 9:40 — Grève des pompiers ignorée, éclipse partout, climatiseurs en panne [ https://substack.com/redirect/8647008f-3ba7-4253-a171-9d9678224d57?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 49:08 — 678 000 comptes fiscaux piratés, timbres et missiles pour l’Ukraine [ https://substack.com/redirect/894f2931-0b61-4233-b6b3-cc85e21cd7c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 1:02:27 — Bayrou plaide la dette qu’il a lui-même creusée [ https://substack.com/redirect/bf846f89-bdac-4205-87ba-3e5db6722bb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Ce qu’on n’entend pas : Epstein, Ceuta, les prisons qui ne sont pas où l’on croit
Les témoins de l’affaire Epstein meurent les uns après les autres avant d’avoir pu témoigner. Une survivante, sur BFM, décrit Paris comme un hub du trafic sexuel organisé via Jean-Luc Brunel et Gérald Marie, et ce que je reproche à la justice française, c’est de laisser ce dernier, seul suspect encore vivant du dossier, tranquille alors que le temps presse. Sur RMC, un auditeur reprend mon analyse de la crise de Ceuta, Maroc, Israël et États-Unis contre l’Espagne, et se fait immédiatement traiter de complotiste par le plateau : la preuve, si besoin était, que ces chaînes fonctionnent comme des chaînes de propagande, les mêmes qui ont évincé la journaliste de RT France Xenia Fedorova. Sur l’USS Abraham Lincoln, des marins tentent de se suicider après 250 jours de mer sans même de savon ; au Royaume-Uni, trois fois plus de citoyens vont en prison pour un post critique du gouvernement que de Russes. Voilà où se loge la vraie censure, loin des éditos sur l’ingérence étrangère.
▶ 53:09 — Une survivante d’Epstein accuse Gérald Marie et pointe l’État français [ https://substack.com/redirect/ac4a34a3-0340-4a08-9d16-1fbfebc8559f?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 1:08:54 — Traité de complotiste pour avoir raison sur Ceuta [ https://substack.com/redirect/6946843b-719f-49c9-88a2-9c8b1ccefa11?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
▶ 1:15:00 — Suicides sur un porte-avions US, prison pour un tweet au Royaume-Uni [ https://substack.com/redirect/cdf39070-d2a1-4c4d-b70f-afc5ff5f522c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Ce qui se joue cet été n’est pas un feuilleton people, c’est une répartition des rôles pour l’année qui vient, et ceux qui écrivent le scénario sont aussi ceux qui le vendent en kiosque.
Video integrale : La vidéo [ https://substack.com/redirect/603073eb-e925-482b-a74a-02470b011534?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Toutes les revues de presse

19daa867d31f2232.subject: Grok Bot is not what you think
19daa867d31f2232.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.bensbites.com/p/grok-bot-is-not-what-you-think

Hey folks,
I had early access to Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/91403e1f-ad25-45c0-9ff1-2c895d7cd14e?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], like many others on X posted. Except, I didn’t actually use it 😬. But since it was publicly launched I have started using it…and, I like it?!
There was a wave of ‘personal agents’ with OpenClaw, then Hermes (not the luxury brand) with many flocking to them. I used them to begin with but then just stopped completely. I can’t quite put my finger on why - one may be because I was just generating shit for the sake of it. Having a shower? Make sure my agent was doing something. Going to sleep? Get my agent on something. Things I used? Zero.
I’m a one-session-at-a-time kinda guy. I hate having to review a ton of agent work (or any work)!
Codex/ChatGPT with its mobile connection was all I needed from an ‘always accessible’ agent that could do stuff on my computer. But Grok Bot’s form factor is slightly different, and it’s pretty nice. 
You ‘personify’ your agents. Each gets a system prompt e.g. “you are ben’s money manager agent”, they can send messages to one another, they have access to their own virtual computer (which you can watch them use), you connect your accounts like Gmail, Calendar, Slack, etc (though I ran into several hiccups trying to connect accounts). 
I think it’s just less is more. There’s a lot less complexity with it, it feels like you’re messaging a teammate in Slack. You can set up automations really easily with it, and you can even go into ‘teach’ the bot by it watching your screen. 
You can effectively do all the same stuff in Codex or Claude, but it’s just a couple of steps more complicated. Maybe I’ll try and mimic the setup in Codex?
Currently, you can only access it if you’re on the $200 plan for Cursor or Grok. And of course Grok Bot is powered by the newly released Grok 4.6… (with 4.7 a couple weeks away). More on that below.
Ben’s Bites is brought to you by Name.com [ https://substack.com/redirect/2ab936ca-ad5e-4afc-9d32-21f434dbe43b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Ship domain integrations in hours with the name.com API [ https://substack.com/redirect/2ab936ca-ad5e-4afc-9d32-21f434dbe43b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. Use the API that powers Vercel, Lovable, and Netlify’s domain services. Built for agents and developers with OpenAPI spec and MCP support. Integrate search, registration, and management. Start building [ https://substack.com/redirect/2ab936ca-ad5e-4afc-9d32-21f434dbe43b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ].
Headlines
Grok 4.6 [ https://substack.com/redirect/eb9e841d-0622-4954-98fc-a894adb582b4?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] is a damn good model. It’s near Sol and Fable’s performance on benchmarks, and it’s way cheaper than both. Also see: Grok 4.6 – A field guide [ https://substack.com/redirect/578ce5e6-7da7-41af-b6c4-f1fa2f5db90b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ].
SpaceX + Cursor is now the #3 frontier lab besides OpenAI and Anthropic (rip Gemini, unless their next model is actually good).
Elon says Grok 4.7 will be ready in the next 3-4 weeks [ https://substack.com/redirect/4fadcf21-36b1-4712-a8e9-ff5a829bd0dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], and it’s currently being post-trained on SpaceX’s company data to make the model best at real-world engineering [ https://substack.com/redirect/ba935c4e-9dff-404e-a909-c4e46df1244e?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], if not everything. The model card for Grok 4.6 [ https://substack.com/redirect/239a0d2d-4595-4f1c-9694-5033b33ccb6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] also covers many benchmarks beyond coding, where it’s either #1 or #2.
ChatGPT now lets you import and sync [ https://substack.com/redirect/0aea6543-7e00-4246-9c7d-23eb01a18cc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] your projects, agent sessions, skills and more from other products like Claude Code.
Your chats started via Claude’s Chrome extension [ https://substack.com/redirect/f8a1001a-3898-4421-8ea4-a0e67cd2b370?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] are now saved in your account and can be accessed from your Desktop, mobile or web app. That also means the Chrome extension chats can do the work you’d usually open Claude Cowrok for.
My Feed
An open source version of Grok Bot [ https://substack.com/redirect/3ca47fc8-73d9-43fc-a44b-87e65081d4a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ].
/interface-review [ https://github.com/jakubkrehel/skills/tree/main/skills/interface-review ] - get a detailed analysis of your UI, typography, layout, colour, writing and accessibility.
/show-me [ https://x.com/dexhorthy/status/2087569590268391897 ] - read less text by making your agent respond in these compact styles to present information - component/file trees, diagrams, pseudocode, and more.
Ref [ https://ref.tools/ ] - shared planning mode for your team before agents start to build the thing. (read more [ https://x.com/reactiverobot/status/2087555397829918918 ])
treg [ https://treg.to/ ] - 2,600 agent-friendly tools for seo/geo, social, leads, ads and more.
Caffeine [ https://github.com/iannuttall/caffeine ] - Keep your Mac awake while you work, then let it sleep when your coding agent waits for you.
Ori Pi [ https://openrouter.ai/ori/harness ] - Run Pi directly on all models available via OpenRouter.
Natter [ https://github.com/iannuttall/natter ] - type anywhere on your Mac using your voice, with live transcription. (how it’s different [ https://x.com/iannuttall/status/2087514192777765173 ])
Ramp AI Index: disappointing adoption of Fable 5 [ https://ramp.com/data/ai-index-august-2026 ].
givemeanode [ https://x.com/evanjconrad/status/2087653501300248658 ] - rent GPUs & CPUs with the infra handled for you and then let your users use them without any worry.
Hone [ https://hone.com/ ] - AI that works towards outcomes that help your company.
Claude fixed my WiFi [ https://x.com/mhudack/status/2087479794099241106 ] from 200 to 810 Mbps.
Vercel is using a software factory of agents [ https://x.com/vercel/status/2087573868877946948 ] to build their AI SDK, with 35% of PRs coming from the factory.
Beating Pangram’s AI detection [ https://x.com/spicey_lemonade/status/2087378273722662999 ] by training a model over the weekend.
How to keep thinking [ https://www.seangoedecke.com/how-to-keep-thinking/ ].
Everything hackable will get hacked [ https://vercel.com/blog/everything-hackable-will-get-hacked ].
A complete guide to AGENTS.md [ https://www.aihero.dev/a-complete-guide-to-agents-md ].

Find me on X [ https://x.com/bentossell/ ], Linkedin [ https://www.linkedin.com/in/ben-tossell-70453537/ ], or YouTube [ https://www.youtube.com/@bentossell694 ]

8947b203409cef6a.subject:
Caitlin Flanagan on AOC and Egg Freezing. Revenge of the Democratic
 Establishment. Plus. . .
8947b203409cef6a.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.thefp.com/p/caitlin-flanagan-aoc-egg-freezing-front-page

It’s Thursday, August 13. This is The Front Page, your daily window into the world of The Free Press—and our take on the world at large. Today: The strange fate of Francesca Hong. What Rod Dreher learned from a Democratic operative. The high school student fighting his classmates’ antisemitism. And much more.
But first: AOC’s race against time.
Heading into the 2026 midterms, the Democratic Party is plotting a rebrand, and 36-year-old congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez is in the center of the action. And while she crisscrosses the country to stump for a new crop of socialist candidates, her personal life has suddenly spilled into view.
Last Saturday, AOC went viral after she posted on Instagram that she had decided to start freezing her eggs. The next day, she went on a Sunday show and took a fertility shot in the green room. And on Monday, TMZ announced that she and her fiancé had split.
Her decision sparked a debate about women preserving their freedom into middle age—but our columnist Caitlin Flanagan has a different take.
“It was like watching the cycle of life in reverse,” she writes. Read Caitlin’s essay on what’s wrong with AOC’s effort to “normalize” egg freezing.
—The Editors
Establishments vs. Insurgents
When DSA-backed Francesca Hong lost her bid for the Wisconsin governorship on Tuesday, much of the press raced toward a premature conclusion. From Bloomberg to National Review, commentators declared that democratic socialism had “hit a wall.” The idea is that the populist movement sweeping the Democratic Party had reached a limit of sorts, rejected by primary voters in a politically moderate state.
Yet look a little closer and you’ll see that it took plenty of effort to make voters spurn her. Today, Audrey Fahlberg reports on how Hong’s opponent, David Crowley, and other moderate Democrats in Wisconsin mobilized to take down Hong with little time left in the race. It’s a comeback that should be studied closely by Democrats around the country who are desperate to halt the socialist surge.
But what gave rise to radicals like Hong in the first place—and how can a party stamp them out before they ever arrive? No one knows that story better than Evan Barker, a former Democratic operative who once worked for Abdul El-Sayed, and who witnessed the takeover of identity politics firsthand. This month, she laid out her takeaways in a new book—and when Rod Dreher read it, the message felt more familiar than he expected. Today, he explains what the Democrats’ turn has taught him about the future of the Republican Party—and how the GOP can avoid falling into the same trap.
And, in case you missed it, read Rupa’s investigation:
MORE FROM THE FREE PRESS
THE NEWS
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to a one-week low [ https://substack.com/redirect/2ef117db-4c0a-4bce-8aa5-f8e83ac43e9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] on Wednesday. The drop came amid increased volatility in the region, as President Donald Trump claimed “total control [ https://substack.com/redirect/aaba76c0-cc64-4313-8663-e41a73aab28a?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]” over the strait, and the Iranian-backed Houthis killed six people [ https://substack.com/redirect/aaba76c0-cc64-4313-8663-e41a73aab28a?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] in the Red Sea.
Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth upset [ https://substack.com/redirect/ded5e0ea-05bb-48d6-a956-c00c8072ccb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] Trump-backed Mike Lindell, of MyPillow fame, to win the Republican nomination for governor on Tuesday. Demuth will run against Senator Amy Klobuchar in the general election.
President Trump announced Wednesday [ https://substack.com/redirect/008b02e1-491f-4c2b-93fe-b81f6fab03dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] that his press secretary Karoline Leavitt is stepping down at the end of August. Leavitt will be leaving to spend time with her two young children, and will remain a top outside adviser to the president’s team.
The Trump administration is set to spend at least $900 million [ https://substack.com/redirect/8448b412-595f-457e-9925-7d897e6481c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] on White House construction by routing funds from other agencies and private donors. The renovation plans include a gilded East Wing ballroom, a new helipad, and a visitor screening center.
Federal authorities arrested a former Southern Poverty Law Center employee, Heidi Beirich, on charges that allege she oversaw [ https://substack.com/redirect/bac0b8e6-47a6-4573-8469-c3222abaf8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] secret payments to informants inside of white supremacist groups. Prosecutors claim Beirich lived with and was romantically involved with one of the recipients. (For more on the scandals rocking SPLC, read Ayaan Hirsi Ali’s essential piece [ https://substack.com/redirect/e087c6b0-09d9-4107-818d-65fe1424a49c?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ].)
Former Disney chief executive Bob Iger and venture capitalist Josh Kushner are buying the Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5 billion [ https://substack.com/redirect/ff519aee-db85-45d9-8b0f-74d7243c682e?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]. Their purchase marks a significant increase from the $10 billion Mark Walter paid for the franchise less than a year prior, despite star player LeBron James’ recent departure [ https://substack.com/redirect/5dbb2fcf-03f1-4958-91e4-1179bc91f8c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ].
A total solar eclipse swept across [ https://substack.com/redirect/55adf34d-87e5-48d0-bfc4-eddd30d5f95b?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] Iceland and Spain, the first to cross mainland Europe since 1999. Spain set up 350 viewing sites amid heat and wildfire warnings, where the eclipse produced a rare “sunset” effect.

2a1697a9f72206be.subject: Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans: Macron annonce une réécriture pour 2027, alors que la censur…
2a1697a9f72206be.body:
View this post on the web at https://alexispoulin.substack.com/p/les-impots-victimes-dun-piratage

Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans: Macron annonce une réécriture pour 2027, alors que la censure vise aussi la vérification d’âge sur laquelle elle reposerait
à lire sur Le Monde Moderne [ https://substack.com/redirect/2d82d885-9446-4bdf-93fc-e21e548e5aac?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ]
Les impôts victimes d’un piratage informatique
Le système d’information du fisc a été victime fin juin d’un “accès illégitime” qui a permis “la consultation et l’extraction de données concernant des particuliers et des professionnels”, a annoncé le ministère de l’Economie et des Finances, sans préciser la nature des données, ni le nombre de contribuables concernés. Le site spécialisé French Breaches, qui documente les cyberattaques commises en France, faisait cependant état de 678 437 personnes qui seraient concernées, dont 392 867 particuliers.
Cette confirmation du piratage par Bercy, près de deux mois après les faits, intervient au lendemain de la revendication par “un acteur malveillant” de cette intrusion dans le système informatique de la Direction générale des Finances publiques “après une usurpation d’identité”, explique le ministère. Bercy assure que “les usagers concernés recevront une information individuelle précisant les données susceptibles d’avoir été consultées ou extraites et, le cas échéant, les mesures de vigilance à adopter”.
Comme c'est systématiquement le cas dans ce type de piratage, la DGFiP “notifiera l'incident à la Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, déposera plainte et communiquera de nouveaux éléments à mesure de l'avancée des investigations”, précise-t-elle.
Notre publication est financée uniquement par ses lecteurs. Pour recevoir les prochains contenus du Monde Moderne, devenez abonné, gratuit ou payant.
Les îles Kouriles : la visite historique de Vladimir Poutine qui irrite le Japon
Pour la première fois depuis son arrivée au pouvoir, Vladimir Poutine s’est rendu dans les îles Kouriles, au cœur d’un contentieux territorial vieux de plus de 80 ans entre la Russie et le Japon. 
Le déplacement a immédiatement fait bondir le Japon. La Première ministre Sanae Takaichi l’a jugé “absolument inacceptable”, estimant qu’il “heurte les sentiments du peuple japonais”, tandis que le ministère nippon des Affaires étrangères a convoqué l’ambassadeur russe. Le gouvernement japonais avait pourtant demandé à plusieurs reprises au Kremlin de renoncer à cette visite. 
Les îles Kouriles [ https://substack.com/redirect/dc5c4263-d48f-4959-a4be-c46789f43ac2?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] forment une longue chaîne volcanique entre la péninsule russe du Kamtchatka et Hokkaido, l’île la plus septentrionale du Japon. Mais le différend entre Moscou et Tokyo porte précisément sur quatre territoires situés au sud de l’archipel : Kounachir, Habomai, Chikotan et Itouroup en russe ; Kunashiri, Habomai, Shikotan et Etorofu en japonais. C’est sur cette dernière île que Vladimir Poutine s’est rendu.
Quelque 20 000 citoyens russes vivent aujourd’hui sur ces îles. Leur intérêt n’est pourtant pas seulement territorial. Le sous-sol abrite notamment des gisements d’or et d’argent et les eaux aux alentours constituent de riches zones de pêche. Une importance économique dont la visite présidentielle a offert une illustration très concrète : à Itouroup, Vladimir Poutine s’est rendu dans une usine de transformation de poisson, où du caviar lui a été offert, ainsi que dans une école. Il a également visité un hôpital.
Mais les Kouriles sont surtout un verrou militaire dans le Pacifique. Pendant la Guerre froide, l’Union soviétique y avait installé des bases aériennes et navales face aux Etats-Unis et au Japon, le principal allié américain dans la région. Cette fonction stratégique n’a pas disparu. 
La dimension militaire était d’ailleurs omniprésente dans le voyage de Vladimir Poutine avant même son arrivée à Itouroup. À Ioujno-Sakhalinsk, sur l’île voisine de Sakhaline, le président russe a présidé une réunion consacrée à la “garantie de la sécurité des frontières orientales de la Russie”. Il est également monté à bord du Varyag, un croiseur lance-missiles de la flotte russe dans le Pacifique, dont il a supervisé des exercices navals.
La veille de sa venue à Itouroup, devant la flotte du Pacifique, Vladimir Poutine avait déjà placé son voyage sur un terrain politique. “Le Japon a identifié la Russie comme l’une des principales sources de menace. Je tiens à souligner que nous ne menaçons pas le Japon. Au contraire, c’est lui qui a des revendications territoriales contre notre pays.” La réponse japonaise a été immédiate. Pour la Première ministre Sanae Takaichi, cet épisode a “encore exacerbé le ressentiment de l’opinion publique japonaise à l’égard de la Russie” et rendu plus difficile toute amélioration des relations bilatérales.
Le ton s’est considérablement durci depuis l’invasion russe de l’Ukraine en février 2022. Le Japon a rejoint les sanctions occidentales contre Moscou et, pour la première fois depuis 2003, a recommencé à qualifier les Kouriles de territoires “occupés illégalement” par la Russie. 
Cette démonstration intervient alors que l’équilibre sécuritaire autour du Japon évolue rapidement. La Russie s’est rapprochée de la Chine : les marines et forces aériennes russes et chinoises conduisent des exercices conjoints dans des zones proches du Japon. 
Un autre front, beaucoup moins visible, relie directement le Japon au conflit ukrainien. Les services de renseignement militaire russes utilisent le Japon comme plaque tournante pour se procurer des composants destinés à l’effort de guerre russe, notamment en profitant des faiblesses de la législation japonaise en matière d’espionnage et de la puissance de son industrie technologique.
Le bras de fer entre le ministère de l’Intérieur et le ministère de la Justice continue
Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, a reçu les directeurs généraux de la police et de la gendarmerie pour préparer des “réponses argumentées” à la note controversée que lui a adressée le garde des Sceaux, Gérald Darmanin, sur le traitement par les enquêteurs des affaires de violences sexuelles sur mineurs. “Ce travail permettra de rétablir certaines vérités”, a-t-il avancé à l'issue de cette réunion. La note avait provoqué la colère des syndicats de policiers, qui ont accusé Gérald Darmanin, ancien ministre de l'Intérieur, de “trahison”. 
“Il y a un certain nombre de choses qui sont dites dans ce document que je vais contester”, avait déjà prévenu le ministre de l’Intérieur en amont de la réunion, assurant vouloir répondre “point par point” mais “de manière constructive, sans aucune polémique”. “Il n’y a pas forcément le nombre de dossiers perdus qui est annoncé”, avait-il notamment affirmé.
Vers un gel partiel des retraites
Le ministre de l’Economie, Roland Lescure, a rouvert le débat autour d’un gel partiel des pensions de retraite pour générer des économies dans le budget 2027. “La question de la contribution des retraités aisés à l’effort de redressement, par exemple par une indexation plus modérée de leurs pensions, mérite d’être posée”, à condition de “préserver les retraités les plus modestes”, a-t-il affirmé dans un entretien à Libération.
Le mécanisme de sous-indexation consiste à revaloriser les pensions de retraite de base à un niveau inférieur à celui de l’inflation, contrairement à ce qui est normalement prévu dans la loi. Un tel dispositif peut être ciblé sur les pensions de retraite les plus élevées. 
Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu avait déjà tenté de geler ces pensions lors de sa proposition initiale de budget pour 2026 afin de dégager près de 3,6 milliards d’euros, mais la mesure n’avait pas été retenue par le Parlement. Même la proposition plus modérée du prédécesseur de François Bayrou, Michel

d8ed2af1acb00162.subject: The War over the WNBA. Plus. . .
d8ed2af1acb00162.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.thefp.com/p/the-war-over-the-wnba-plus

It’s Friday, August 14. This is The Front Page, your daily window into the world of The Free Press—and our take on the world at large. Today: Suzy Weiss on the First Amendment war over face tattoos. Tyler Cowen on how Donald Trump’s immigration stance puts conservative values at risk. And much more.
But first: how Caitlin Clark became a culture war piñata.
I’ve been watching the WNBA for a couple of decades now, going back to Rebecca Lobo and Lisa Leslie, to the more recent era of Tamika Catchings and Diana Taurasi. They were all great players, but there’s a decent chance you’ve never heard of them, even if you’re a sports fan. Only die-hard women’s basketball fans watched the WNBA, and there weren’t very many of us.
But three years ago Caitlin Clark, with her amazing long-range shots and gorgeous blind passes, joined the league and became its first breakout superstar. On the one hand, her astonishing popularity has done wonders for the WNBA, bringing with it higher player salaries, a $200 million TV deal, and a status quo in which teams fly on private jets instead of commercial flights.
On the other hand, her popularity has had a dark side. The heightened scrutiny of Clark, her team, and the league has led to culture war after culture war in the WNBA—an organization that was woke before people used the term woke.
Clark’s popularity, in a majority-black sport, has led to accusations of racism. Her teammate Sophie Cunningham [ https://substack.com/redirect/26d981c5-7122-4e87-b621-a82d26761c22?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ] has been dragged for saying it’s “common sense” to exclude trans women from the league. Two former NBA players, Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White, have declared that they’ve decided they are women and plan to offer themselves up in the draft—a stunt apparently designed to expose the WNBA’s hypocrisy on the trans issue. Though a WNBA task force met this week to come up with a definition for woman, the meeting ended, astonishingly, with no decision.
I spent some time this week trying to learn whether the WNBA would be able to get past its culture war controversies—or whether the controversies would do it serious damage. Read my story to see where I came out.
—Joe Nocera
EDITORS’ PICKS
As the whole internet now knows, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, at the age of 36, is freezing her eggs. She shared her decision on social media in the hope that it would “normalize” the process. But Caitlin Flanagan, in her latest essay, argues that if we’re raising awareness of egg freezing, we should raise awareness of its success rates. “The truth is that many, many times, egg freezing can lead to heartbreak because it’s hardly foolproof, or even a likely way to get pregnant.”
Critics accused AOC of putting career ahead of starting a family—the latest pile-on to prove that the cultural tide has turned against the girlboss. To make sense of the backlash, Rafaela Siewert interviewed sex researcher Dr. Debra Soh. Don’t miss their conversation on AOC’s gambit to have it all, why more women are choosing to become single moms, and why America just can’t quit its trad wife obsession.
Meanwhile, Zoomers who leave their love lives to the optimizing forces of the algorithm are finding themselves worse off. This week, Kara Kennedy reported on the young people who are fed up with dating apps—and the dreamers reinventing romance for a post-app world. Meet the AI matchmakers, the “dating doc” writers, and the people stapling personal ads to telephone poles.
A blockbuster from Rupa Subramanya dropped this week: her investigation into the Virginia high school where antisemitic bullying, allegedly mostly by Muslim boys, went unpunished by administrators—until the state attorney general’s office stepped in. Rupa’s story caught the attention of Harmeet Dhillon, the head of the Justice Department’s civil rights division, who posted on X [ https://substack.com/redirect/cf19b0ba-c6ea-4497-83c0-78a3c9178a8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMmU2aDEifQ.VGKrlpe010xZBcMagL3trNwkDdJUfw_qmH45MbfoDHA ], “This is concerning. We are looking into it.”
Finally, New York magazine’s most recent cover story christened the Big Apple “Habibi City,” celebrating a community of Middle Easterners “flexing their cultural clout.” Not so fast, writes Liel Leibovitz—himself a Middle Eastern immigrant—who sees something darker afoot than vapid ethno-narcissism. Habibi City, he argues, sees itself as an “oppositional force, here to fight against all of America’s many transgressions, with the goal being the remaking of America in their own image.”
